bihar_raw_news.title: Maharashtra govt tightens eligibility for professor, dean posts in medical colleges - ET Education
bihar_raw_news.content: Industry 1 min Read Maharashtra govt tightens eligibility for professor, dean posts in medical colleges Maharashtra has revised recruitment rules for senior posts in government medical colleges, making promotions the route for appointing professors, deans and joint directors. The changes also specify experience requirements and limit direct recruitment opportunities for outside candidates. AP Published On Nov 25, 2026 at 11:07 AM IST Read by 5039 Professionals Set ETEducation as your preferred source on Google Share Icon Copy Link Share on Whatsapp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook Bookmark Comment Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis Mumbai: Senior posts in Maharashtra’s government medical education system, including professors, deans and joint directors, will be filled through promotion under recruitment rules notified by the Medical Education Department. The move will narrow opportunities for candidates outside government system to enter these positions directly. Under the revised rules, associate professors with at least three years’ experience in the relevant subject will be eligible for promotion as professors. For appointment as dean, candidates must have served as professors in govt medical colleges for at least five years and have a total of 10 years’ teaching experience in a medical institution. The joint director’s post will be filled through promotion, based on seniority, from among deans with at least three years’ experience. At the associate professor level, half the posts will be filled through promotion and the remaining half through direct recruitment on the recommendations of the Maharashtra Public Service Commission (MPSC). Assistant professors will continue to be recruited directly through the commission. The changes have drawn criticism over the reduced scope for recruiting experienced teachers and researchers from outside govt medical colleges. Critics have also questioned the emphasis on seniority in appointments to academic and administrative leadership positions. Comments What are your thoughts?

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar targets one crore litres of daily milk production by 2030: CM Samrat Chaudhary
bihar_raw_news.content: National Bihar targets one crore litres of daily milk production by 2030: CM Samrat Chaudhary On Nov 26, 2026 Share Patna, Nov 26 (IANS) Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Chaudhary on Thursday announced an ambitious target of increasing the state’s daily milk production from the current 48 lakh litres to one crore litres by 2030, emphasising that the dairy sector would play a crucial role in strengthening the rural economy and empowering women. Addressing the National Milk Day-2026 celebrations, jointly inaugurated by Samrat Chaudhary and Union Minister for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry, Dairying and Panchayati Raj Rajiv Ranjan Singh, alias Lalan Singh, the Chief Minister said the Bihar government was committed to making the state self-reliant in milk production and placing it among the country’s leading milk-producing states. He said milk production was an important foundation for farmers’ prosperity, rural economic development and women’s financial independence. Highlighting India’s achievements in the dairy sector, Samrat said that under Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s leadership, the country’s milk production had nearly doubled over the past 12 years. India currently contributes approximately 25 per cent of global milk production, reflecting the efforts of livestock farmers and people associated with the dairy industry. To achieve Bihar’s production target, the government will strengthen infrastructure related to animal husbandry, dairy development and milk procurement. Under the Mukhyamantri Gaudhan Yojana, financial assistance is being provided to farmers for purchasing high-quality cows and buffaloes. The initiative is expected to promote self-employment and increase milk production through improved breeds. The Chief Minister also praised the performance of the Bihar State Milk Cooperative Federation, saying its Sudha brand had established a strong reputation for quality and reliability across the country. He said Sudha had established a milk processing unit with a capacity of one lakh litres in Assam, while a similar facility would soon be launched in West Bengal. These initiatives would expand markets for Bihar’s dairy producers and generate additional economic opportunities. He added that traditional Bihari products would also be marketed under the Sudha brand. Products such as makhana kheer and rabri have already been introduced to consumers, helping promote local products while increasing milk consumption. Samrat further announced that the government would promote goat rearing alongside cow and buffalo farming. A target has been set to collect and market one lakh litres of goat milk daily through the Sudha network. Emphasising women’s participation, he said Pashu Sakhis were being trained to provide guidance and assistance to livestock farmers. The government aims to make one crore women in Bihar Lakhpati Didis by 2030, of whom 50 lakh have already achieved the target. The Chief Minister also highlighted plans to promote organic manure production using livestock waste and encourage compressed biogas projects under Bihar’s CBG policy. He said veterinary clinics would be established in every administrative block to ensure better healthcare facilities for livestock. Describing Samastipur as Bihar’s leading milk-producing district, he urged other districts to follow its example. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar plans to integrate AI across public healthcare delivery system - Medical Buyer
bihar_raw_news.content: In a major step to strengthen technology-driven healthcare, the Bihar government has outlined plans to integrate AI across its public healthcare delivery system. The proposed AI-driven initiative will cover several critical areas, spanning medical diagnostics, medicine supply management, telemedicine, hospital bed monitoring, and emergency response services. Outlining the roadmap during a recent event, Bihar Health Minister Nishant Kumar said, “AI is a defining feature of today’s changing world and a necessity for the future. Alongside its personal use, we also need to pay serious attention to its institutional use. In this direction, work is underway in Bihar to explore the possibilities of using AI systematically and effectively to improve healthcare services.” The initiative aims to bridge the urban-rural divide by connecting existing healthcare infrastructure with digital technologies. Key focus areas Under the proposed roadmap, the state plans to use AI to analyse X-rays, CT scans, MRI and ultrasound images, enabling healthcare professionals to identify preliminary indicators of diseases such as tuberculosis and cancer. Health Minister Nishant Kumar also called for an audit of diagnostic equipment available at medical college hospitals and district hospitals to assess their availability, utilisation and operational status. Additionally, the state plans to use barcodes, QR codes, batch numbers and clinical data to track medicine supplies, verify authenticity, monitor doctor availability and detect distribution irregularities. “In Bihar, efforts are underway to better integrate digital systems such as BHAVYA, BHAVYA Lite and mASHA, analyse data, and make the Smart Ambulance, Patient Referral System and Real-Time Bed Management more effective,” he added. To improve access to specialist healthcare in rural areas, the government plans to strengthen AI-enabled telemedicine services and clinical decision support. The initiative is expected to connect patients at rural health centres with specialist doctors, reducing the need for economically weaker families to travel to major cities for medical consultations. Another major focus is the development of a digital hospital bed management system providing real-time information about vacant and occupied beds in general wards, Intensive Care Units (ICUs), High Dependency Units (HDUs), and other critical care facilities. The system is intended to help patients and referring hospitals identify facilities with available beds before transferring critically ill patients, and reduce delays in accessing emergency care. Further, as part of its emergency healthcare plans, the state is exploring a pilot project involving two to four AI-enabled smart ambulances equipped with digital ECG machines, blood pressure monitors, pulse oximeters, and GPS-based tracking systems. The AI-enabled systems are intended to record patient vitals, enable real-time data sharing and video consultations with specialists, and transmit medical information to hospitals ahead of arrival to support timely treatment. The Health Minister further called for integrating the ambulances with trauma centres and super-speciality hospitals to identify suitable facilities based on bed availability, ICU capacity, imaging services and specialist availability. The latest development builds on the State’s ongoing efforts to improve emergency response, patient tracking and coordination across public healthcare facilities through technology. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar plans 31 new medical colleges, aims to double MBBS seats to 10K by 2030
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar plans 31 new medical colleges, aims to double MBBS seats to 10K by 2030 Subscribe to Notifications Written By : Divyani Paul Published On 2026-11-26 04:00 GMT | Update On 2026-11-26 04:00 GMT Patna- With the goal of increasing the total number of MBBS seats in Bihar from 5,000 to 10,000 by 2030, Chief Minister Samrat Chaudhary announced recently that the Bihar government has planned to establish 31 new medical colleges across the state over the next three years. This announcement was made while speaking as the chief guest at a 'White Coat Ceremony' held for the first batch of a private medical college in Daraunda, Siwan district. He also presented a comprehensive roadmap for the expansion of healthcare and higher education in the state. Also Read: Madhya Pradesh plans 22 new medical colleges, MBBS seats to rise to 18,050 According to the TOI media news report, Chaudhary stated, "We have a plan to establish 15 brownfield and 16 greenfield medical colleges in the next three years." To meet the needs of the state’s dense population of approximately 140 million, the government will employ a Public-Private Partnership ( PPP) model to accelerate infrastructure development. Furthermore, the construction of the government medical college in Siwan is set to be completed by 2027. Currently, there are a total of 31 medical colleges operating in Bihar; of these, 14 are government-run and 17 are private institutions. Furthermore, the Chief Minister also emphasised the need to reduce the number of students leaving Bihar for higher education. He noted that, under the 'Student Credit Card Scheme', the state government spends approximately ₹18,000 crore annually to cover tuition fees for students attending educational institutions in other states. Moreover, the government aims to ensure that there is at least one university in every district of Bihar within the next three to four years. In this regard, the state government has recently approved five new public universities (including the V.V. Giri University in Siwan) and four private universities. This initiative represents a significant effort toward transforming Bihar into a self-reliant educational hub. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Holds First e-Cabinet Meeting, Clears 34 Proposals - Elets eGov
bihar_raw_news.content: Home · Digital governance Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary. Photo: IPRD Bihar via Wikimedia Commons The Bihar e-Cabinet system went live on 25 November 2026, when Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary chaired the state’s first paperless meeting of the Council of Ministers in Patna. Cabinet agendas, proposals and decisions are now handled online, and Bihar has become the 12th Indian state to run cabinet business digitally. The rollout comes three weeks after the Chief Minister ordered an early move to a fully digital cabinet . The first e-Cabinet sitting cleared 34 proposals from several departments. How the Bihar e-Cabinet works Arvind Kumar Chaudhary, Additional Chief Secretary of the Cabinet Secretariat Department, briefed reporters after the meeting, according to the PTI-Bhasha report . The key features are: Paperless workflow: cabinet agendas, proposals and decisions are prepared, shared and recorded through a digital software platform Devices for ministers: every minister has been given an iPad to read cabinet papers, and ministers still attend meetings in person Cost and payback: the iPads cost about ₹2 crore, and the state expects savings on paper to recover that amount within six to seven months Platform: e-Cabinet systems in Indian states are mainly built on a digital platform developed by the National Informatics Centre (NIC) The government says the system will make cabinet work faster, more secure, more transparent and more effective, while cutting the bulky printed files that used to reach ministers before every meeting. What the first e-Cabinet meeting approved As reported by Live Hindustan , the decisions taken at the first paperless sitting include: An administrative sanction of ₹1,794.32 crore for Patna’s water supply, covering 75 wards and more than 2.18 lakh households A six-fold rise in the annual administrative grant for Gram Kachahris, from ₹4,000 to ₹24,000, from 1 April 2027 Setting up a Bihar Economic Advisory Council to support policy-making A “Bihar Hai Taiyar” image campaign through the Bihar Foundation, and Bihar Business Connect-2027 in February 2027 Bihar’s wider digital governance push The e-Cabinet joins a run of recent reforms in the state, including virtual hearings in all 899 revenue courts , the UPYOG portal linking 264 urban local bodies and a Revenue Department portal to track House questions . Himachal Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Arunachal Pradesh, Tripura, Andhra Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh are among the states that adopted a paperless cabinet before Bihar. Legislatures are moving the same way, with assemblies such as Chhattisgarh going paperless through NeVA . Key takeaways Bihar held its first e-Cabinet meeting on 25 November 2026, chaired by CM Samrat Choudhary. Bihar is the 12th state to run cabinet business online, with iPads issued to all ministers. The ₹2 crore spent on devices is expected to be recovered through paper savings in six to seven months. The power ministry is likely to propose the addition of 80.6 million ' superior voting rights ' shares and 806 million redeemable preference shares to secure, respectively, 51% voting rights and a 51.75% stake in the paid-up capital of the merged entity, said the people cited above. The Centre currently owns 55.99% shares in PFC but does not directly own any stock in REC , which is a subsidiary of PFC. With a market capitalisation of about ₹1.1 lakh crore, PFC owns 52.63% in REC, which has a market value of about ₹79,000 crore. Live Events Fresh Investments After the merger, the government holding in the merged entity will fall to 42.02% with the announced swap ratio of 0.88. Fresh investments from the government, so that it owns 51.75% in the merged entity with the requisite voting control, could be around Rs 7,500-8,000 crore in this arrangement, said the people cited above. Superior voting rights shares are equity shares that carry more votes per share than ordinary equity shares. bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar News: Rajgir Zoo & Nature Safari to Receive Prestigious SKOCH Award for Eco-Tourism and Innovation Bihar's Rajgir Zoo and Nature Safari are honoured with the SKOCH Award for sustainable eco-tourism and governance innovation. The facilities integrate conservation, biodiversity education, and modern technology to enhance visitor experience while protecting wildlife. India -Oneindia Staff By Oneindia Staff Published: Thursday, November 26, 2026, 18:01 [IST] Add as a preferred source on Google Patna, Nov 26:* Bihar's efforts in eco-tourism and wildlife conservation are set to receive another major national recognition. Rajgir Zoo and Nature Safari will be honoured with the prestigious SKOCH Award for its initiatives in sustainable eco-tourism and innovation in governance. The award will be presented at a ceremony in New Delhi on December 19, 2026. The achievement will bring further recognition to the state's efforts to promote tourism alongside environmental conservation under the leadership of Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary. AI Summary AI-generated summary, reviewed by editors Bihar's Rajgir Zoo and Nature Safari are honoured with the SKOCH Award for sustainable eco-tourism and governance innovation. The facilities integrate conservation, biodiversity education, and modern technology to enhance visitor experience while protecting wildlife. Switch To Shorts The government has made a unique effort to ensure that Rajgir Zoo and Nature Safari are not confined to tourism and entertainment. They are also integrated with wildlife conservation, biodiversity and environmental education. Spread across approximately 191.12 hectares, Rajgir Zoo Safari is Bihar's first zoo safari, inaugurated on February 16, 2022. Separate safari zones have been developed for lions, tigers, bears, leopards and herbivorous animals. Facilities such as an exotic aviary, a 180-degree theatre and an open-air theatre have also become major attractions for visitors. A unique blend of adventure and nature Rajgir Nature Safari, spread across approximately 550 hectares, offers visitors an exciting experience amidst nature. Facilities developed here include a glass skywalk bridge, a suspension bridge, zipline, sky biking, a butterfly park, a medicinal plant garden and a cactus garden. These activities promote tourism while also creating awareness about nature and environmental conservation. Modern technology strengthens management Modern technology is being used extensively at the zoo and nature safari to ensure visitor convenience and wildlife safety. Facilities such as QR code-based ticketing, slot management, real-time GPS tracking of safari vehicles, a central control room and CCTV surveillance have been implemented. Digital storytelling and interactive platforms are also used to educate visitors about biodiversity and wildlife conservation. In recognition of the effective use of technology, Zoo Safari Director Ram Sundar M was conferred the "Best Use of Technology" award in September. Eco-tourism visitors rise over two years According to data from the Environment, Forest and Climate Change Department, the number of tourists visiting eco-tourism destinations across Bihar increased from 55.20 lakh in 2022-23 to 74.90 lakh in 2024-25. Over the same period, visitors to Rajgir Nature Safari rose from approximately 1.59 lakh to 3 lakh. bihar_raw_news.title: India Produces 253.81 Million Tonnes of Milk in 2025-26: BAHS Report - DD India
bihar_raw_news.content: Top Stories of the Day Share DD India November 26, 2026 7:57 PM IST India Produces 253.81 Million Tonnes of Milk in 2025-26: BAHS Report Author: DD India National Milk Day 2026 was celebrated in Patna, Bihar, on Thursday, with the launch of several initiatives and the dedication of major dairy and livestock infrastructure projects aimed at strengthening India’s dairy sector and improving farmers’ incomes. Addressing the gathering, Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary highlighted the contribution of livestock farmers to Bihar’s rural economy and said the state government was committed to strengthening dairy and animal husbandry infrastructure. He said Bihar currently produces around 48 lakh litres of milk daily and has set a target of increasing production to one crore litres per day. Union Minister Lalan Singh said India contributes approximately one-fourth of global milk production and has registered an increase of around 84 per cent in milk production compared to 2013-14. He also highlighted India’s position as the world’s second-largest producer of eggs and fourth-largest producer of meat. Highlighting Bihar’s dairy sector growth, the Union Minister said the state’s milk production increased from 7.19 million metric tonnes in 2013-14 to 13.76 million metric tonnes in 2025-26, registering growth of around 91 per cent. He also noted that COMFED’s daily milk procurement had reached 23.97 lakh kg, while daily sales stood at 18.41 lakh litres. The minister underlined the role of government initiatives, including the National Animal Disease Control Programme, Rashtriya Gokul Mission and National Programme for Dairy Development, in strengthening animal healthcare, livestock breeding and dairy cooperatives. National Gopal Ratna Awards presented The National Gopal Ratna Awards 2026 were conferred on individuals and organisations for their outstanding contributions to indigenous cattle and buffalo breed conservation, dairy development and livestock productivity. The awards recognised achievements in three categories: Best Dairy Farmer Rearing Indigenous Cattle/Buffalo Breeds, Best Artificial Insemination Technician and Best Dairy Cooperative Society, Milk Producer Company or Dairy Farmer Producer Organisation. Special awards were also presented to winners from the North Eastern Region and Himalayan States. Basic Animal Husbandry Statistics 2026 released The Basic Animal Husbandry Statistics (BAHS) 2026 was also released during the celebration. Based on the Integrated Sample Survey conducted between March 1, 2025, and February 28, 2026, the report estimates India’s milk production at 253.81 million tonnes in 2025-26. The country’s egg production was estimated at 156.88 billion, while total meat production stood at 10.63 million tonnes, including 5.13 million tonnes of poultry meat. Dairy infrastructure and new initiatives launched Several infrastructure projects were inaugurated and dedicated to the nation, including Data Processing and Milk Collection Units for dairy cooperative societies, Mineral Mixture Plants at Patna and Muzaffarpur, and an Effluent Treatment Plant at Mithila Milk Union in Samastipur. A milk processing plant of Namaste India, with a capacity of two lakh litres per day, was also dedicated to the nation at Sikandarpur, Bihta, Patna. bihar_raw_news.content: West Bengal Finmin Swapan Dasgupta at ET Bengal Ascends West Bengal is looking to rebuild investor confidence by addressing concerns over land availability, labour practices and business environment, and restore economic growth because "nothing succeeds like success," state finance minister Swapan Dasgupta told Deepshikha Sikarwar during a fireside chat at ET Bengal Ascends . He discussed the challenge of tackling labour syndication, bringing skilled talent back to the state and managing debt of around ₹8 lakh crore. Also Read | ET Bengal Ascends: CM Suvendu Adhikari pitches a middle path to unlock land for industry Edited excerpts: Your government came to power six months back. How has the experience been of the 'double-engine' sarkar? Live Events There is a lot of curiosity, a lot of expectation, a lot of optimism and goodwill shown by the people who for different reasons with great regret left West Bengal. They are the people who are providing the goodwill and impetus for revival and telling us you got to do something. That itself is the most reassuring part of our job in the past six months. You said the narrative about Bengal needs a change. What does Bengal ascending look like for the next five years? How do you break this narrative? Firstly, nothing succeeds like success. What we need is to immediately tell people that there is hope, it is not inevitable that all the young people in West Bengal will leave the state, and that it is possible for investment to come into West Bengal. It is possible for entrepreneurs within the state to actually do well. So, you ought to create systems. Now, we need to go to the assembly and get it done...by the end of the year. The abolition of urban land ceiling is just one step. The next one - acquisition of land in rural areas for industry - is difficult because of complex tenancy laws. Those things have to be changed. You need political muscle and political confidence to be able to do that. I believe the repeal of the urban land ceiling act will trigger a real estate boom...and that will take real estate out of the hands of people who just monopolise and terrorise people. Once the organised sector comes in line with what is happening in the rest of the country, things will fall in place. national_raw_news.title: US proposes fresh tariffs on imports from 14 economies, including India
national_raw_news.content: United States has proposed fresh tariffs ranging from 15 to 35 per cent on imports from 14 economies, including China, the European Union and India. The other economies covered include Taiwan, Singapore, Switzerland, Indonesia, Malaysia, Cambodia, Thailand, South Korea, Bangladesh and Japan. US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer today said the proposed measures are aimed at addressing policies that Washington believes disadvantage American manufacturers and weaken the country’s industrial base. China could face tariffs of up to 40 per cent, while Vietnam may face duties of up to 35 per cent. The proposals include exemptions for certain products, such as semiconductors and other high-tech goods from Taiwan and South Korea. The duties will not take effect immediately. For India, the USTR has proposed tariffs of up to 25 per cent on goods, after accounting for existing Section 301 duties, with exemptions for certain products. It has also proposed considering a 17 per cent rate if India reaches a reciprocal trade agreement with the US that addresses the findings of the investigation. The US administration has invited public comments until 5th January next year, with hearings scheduled to begin on 25th January. The proposed tariffs could come into force as early as February next year. Meanwhile, the European Union and China have rejected Washington’s allegations of excessive industrial production. The European Commission said it would examine Washington’s justification for the move. It noted that tariffs on European goods are capped at 15 per cent under the existing trade agreement with the United States.

national_raw_news.title: India wins Best National Pavilion – Visitors’ Lion award at Venice Art Biennale
national_raw_news.content: India has won the Best National Pavilion – Visitors’ Lion at the Venice Art Biennale, the Olympics of the art world. The honour was decided through votes by visitors from across the globe and is a recognition of India’s growing cultural influence. Expressing happiness, Prime Minister Narendra Modi called it a proud moment for India’s art and cultural world. In a social media post, Prime Minister Modi said India’s artists are bringing fresh perspectives to the world of art, drawing inspiration from India’s rich and diverse cultural heritage. He wished that this feat would inspire many more young Indians to pursue art and explore new creative horizons. Culture and Tourism Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat has said, this global recognition is a testament to the talent of new-age Indian artists and the vibrancy of the nation’s contemporary art scene. He said, this award celebrates how India’s timeless artistic traditions can find powerful contemporary expression and resonate with audiences across the world. Mr Shekhawat said that the honour will inspire generations of Indian artists to engage with the world with greater confidence and creativity. Housed at the historic Arsenale, the India Pavilion was commissioned by the National Gallery of Modern Art, Ministry of Culture, with the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts serving as the executing agency.

national_raw_news.title: PM Modi calls for strengthening constitutional values and placing India First in national endeavours
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said that over the past decade, Government has laid special emphasis on Kartavya, or the duties of a citizen. He said, Indian civilisation has always emphasised the responsibilities that accompany every role in society. In an op-ed in daily newspapers in English and Hindi today on Constitution Day, Mr Modi said, the spirit of Kartavya has found expression in several mass movements, from Swachh Bharat to water conservation and environmental protection. Prime Minister Narendra Modi today called upon citizens to uphold the spirit of the Constitution and work collectively towards building a developed India by 2047. In an op-ed in daily newspapers in English and Hindi Mr Modi recalled the adoption of the Constitution in 1949. He noted that the Constitution must find resonance beyond Parliament and the courts and become an integral part of the collective consciousness of citizens, particularly the youth. He said the decision to observe 26 November as Constitution Day was aimed at deepening people’s connection with the Constitution. Paying tribute to Dr. Rajendra Prasad, Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar and all members of the Constituent Assembly, Mr Modi said that their greatness lay in drawing extensively from the rich traditions and civilisational wisdom of Bharat while framing a modern Constitution. He emphasised that it is important that the Constitution have a resonance far beyond the precincts of Parliament and the courts. Sharing his personal journey, the Prime Minister said the Constitution had made it possible for a person born into a family of modest means, with no privileges or advantages of birth, to shoulder the responsibility of serving the world’s largest democracy. Mr. Modi described various government initiatives, including PM Awas Yojana, Ujjwala Yojana, Ayushman Bharat, MUDRA and PM-SVANidhi, as measures aimed at improving the lives of disadvantaged sections and expanding opportunities. Referring to a recent World Bank report, the Prime Minister said nearly 50 crore Indians had moved out of poverty. He noted that digital technology and platforms like UPI transcend all divides and place opportunities once available to a privileged few within the reach of every citizen, advancing the constitutional ideal of inclusivity. Mr. Modi said the abrogation of Articles 370 and 35A in 2019 enabled the full implementation of the Constitution in Jammu and Kashmir, extending constitutional rights to all sections of society. Highlighting the successful elimination of Naxalism, the Prime Minister said that the government has ensured that the poorest of the poor can finally exercise their constitutional rights without fear. Mr Modi further added that the journey of our Constitution would be incomplete without recognising the remarkable women who helped shape it. Mr Modi accused the Opposition of seeking to curtail reservation for Other Backward Classes (OBC) to introduce quotas for Muslims. He said, it is most appalling that the biggest party in the Opposition wants to reduce OBC reservation and bring Muslim reservations, something the makers of the Constitution, notably Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar, were totally against. The Prime Minister said, the country’s constitutional democracy has a clearly defined role for the Opposition. He said, sadly, the leading Opposition party seems to have become more of an obstructionist than a opposition. Mr Modi said, they should know that disrupting democratic processes is no substitute for discharging constitutional responsibilities.

national_raw_news.content: The Constitution Day (Samvidhan Diwas) is being observed today to commemorate the adoption of the Constitution of India by the Constituent Assembly on 26th November, 1949. The day has been observed as Constitution Day since 2015. Constitution Day provides an occasion to reflect upon the principles and values enshrined in the Constitution of India and to renew the collective commitment to its ideals. The observance seeks to strengthen constitutional awareness, promote responsible citizenship and encourage active participation in upholding the democratic values of the nation. On the occasion, the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs is facilitating an online reading of the Preamble to the Constitution through the MyGov portal in 23 languages, comprising 22 Scheduled Languages and English. This initiative will provide an opportunity to citizens across the country to read the Preamble and reaffirm their commitment to the ideals and values enshrined in the Constitution. Various activities are being organised across the country by Ministries and Departments of the Government, State and Union Territories Governments, autonomous bodies and institutions to mark the occasion. These activities include collective reading of the Preamble, seminars, webinars, quizzes, essay and debate competitions, poster-making, cultural programmes, awareness campaigns, walks, runs and other community engagement activities. The Ministry noted that various awareness and outreach activities are also being undertaken through digital platforms and community-based initiatives to promote understanding of the Constitution and its significance in the country’s democratic framework.

national_raw_news.title: WAVES Film Bazaar at IFFI in Goa attracts 2,288 delegates from 54 countries
national_raw_news.content: In the ongoing International Film Festival of India (IFFI), in Goa, key outcomes were announced yesterday from the recently concluded WAVES Film Bazaar, alongside vibrant cultural celebrations and special sessions honouring legendary voices of Indian cinema. In today’s events, exciting masterclasses and special film screenings are lined up promising another engaging chapter in the festival. Two Letters of Intent for India-Chile co-productions have emerged as a major outcome of the 20th edition of the WAVES Film Bazaar, while 14 Memoranda of Understanding and agreements are nearing finalisation. Addressing a press conference in Goa yesterday, Additional Secretary in the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Prabhat, said that WAVES Film Bazaar brought together 2 thousand 288 delegates from 54 countries, including 471 buyers. He added that the Bazaar also facilitated around 220 business-to-business meetings, this year. The festival also experienced a colourful IFFI Parade in Panaji, celebrating Goa’s cultural heritage through vibrant floats and folk performances. While the Aakash Kandil Competition added a creative spark to the celebrations, showcasing colourful lanterns inspired by IFFI’s Peacock mascot. The 6th day also witnessed acclaimed playback singer K. S. Chithra paying tributes to legendary singers Lata Mangeshkar, Asha Bhosle and S. Janaki during a special session. Meanwhile, today, the seventh day promises an exciting line-up of events, including masterclasses by casting director Mukesh Chhabra on auditioning and actor selection, and Natalie Wade of the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences on the Academy Awards. Special screenings will include Rishab Shetty’s Kantara: A Legend Chapter 1, and the Marathi film Tu Aahes Na as a gala presentation

national_raw_news.title: Constitution Day to Be Observed Across India on November 26
national_raw_news.content: Constitution Day, or Samvidhan Diwas, will be observed across the country on November 26 to mark the adoption of the Constitution of India by the Constituent Assembly on November 26, 1949. The day has been observed as Constitution Day since 2015 to promote awareness about the Constitution and reaffirm the country’s commitment to its democratic values and principles. As part of this year’s celebrations, the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs is facilitating an online reading of the Preamble to the Constitution through the MyGov portal in 23 languages, including 22 Scheduled Languages and English. Citizens can participate by reading the Preamble, downloading a participation certificate and sharing it on social media. The celebrations also include a Constitution Quiz being conducted through the MyGov and MyBharat portals from November 18 to 26. In addition, Viksit Bharat Yuva Samvad is being organised across 786 districts in all 36 States and Union Territories from November 24 to 26 to encourage greater participation among young people. Several activities are being organised by Central Ministries and Departments, State and Union Territory governments, educational institutions and other organisations. These include collective readings of the Preamble, seminars, webinars, quizzes, essay and debate competitions, poster-making, cultural programmes, awareness campaigns, walks and community engagement initiatives. Schools, colleges and universities have also been encouraged to organise special morning assemblies, discussions and competitions to familiarise students with the making of the Constitution and its key features. With a special focus on grassroots participation, the celebrations aim to strengthen constitutional awareness among citizens, particularly young people and students, through digital platforms and community-based outreach programmes. Constitution Day serves as an occasion to reflect on the ideals of justice, liberty, equality and fraternity enshrined in the Constitution and renew the collective commitment to upholding the country’s democratic framework.

national_raw_news.title: PM chairs 55th PRAGATI meeting
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister's Office PM chairs 55th PRAGATI meeting PM reviews five infrastructure projects in the road, power, coal and railway sectors worth over ₹78,000 crore PM stresses on timely execution accompanied by high standards of construction quality PM also reviews the ITI ecosystem including the implementation of PM-SETU PM calls for stronger PSU–ITI linkages and skilling aligned with industrial clusters and sectoral needs PM advocates the 3C approach of Classroom–Company–Career to connect training with employment PM notes that stronger links between ITIs and local employers could expand employment opportunities closer to home Posted On: 25 NOV 2026 9:07PM by PIB Delhi Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi chaired the 55th meeting of PRAGATI, the ICT-enabled, multi-modal platform aimed at fostering Pro-Active Governance and Timely Implementation, at Seva Teerth earlier today. The platform brings together the Central and State Governments to address implementation bottlenecks and improve the delivery of projects and welfare schemes. During the meeting, the Prime Minister reviewed five critical infrastructure projects in the road, power, coal and railway sectors, with a total cost of over ₹78,000 crore. He also reviewed the Industrial Training Institute (ITI) ecosystem, including the implementation of the Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs (PM-SETU). Prime Minister emphasised that delays in infrastructure projects have consequences beyond cost escalation, as they postpone the benefits intended for citizens, businesses and the economy. He called upon the concerned Ministries and State Governments to resolve pending issues with clear responsibility and realistic timelines. He stressed that timely execution must be accompanied by high standards of construction quality. Reviewing the road project, the Prime Minister called for expeditious implementation and reiterated the need to focus on outcomes over outlays. While reviewing the coal project, the Prime Minister emphasised that rehabilitation and resettlement should be undertaken in a timely and dignified manner alongside timely project implementation. While reviewing the power project, the Prime Minister suggested exploring innovative models for decentralised solar and wind power projects. He emphasised that such projects should be developed closer to centres of consumption wherever feasible, taking into account local resource availability and demand. These efforts should aim to improve the availability of reliable and affordable power and ease pressure on transmission infrastructure. Reviewing the ITI ecosystem and the implementation of PM-SETU, Prime Minister called upon Chief Ministers and Chief Secretaries to provide leadership in strengthening ITIs and deepening industry participation under PM-SETU. He emphasised that this was an opportune time for industry to partner with ITIs, contribute to their upgradation and help align training with current and future manpower requirements. He called for close collaboration between States, ITIs and industry to translate these partnerships into better training and employment opportunities for young people. Prime Minister called upon Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) to assess their future manpower requirements and strengthen linkages with ITIs for training and recruitment in relevant trades.
